entities.name: Church of Sweden
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Church of Sweden (Svenska kyrkan), founded as a Lutheran church in 1527 under King Gustav Vasa's Reformation (which appropriated Catholic Church property to fund the Swedish state), was the state church of Sweden until 2000 — when Sweden became the last Scandinavian country to separate church and state, ending 473 years of established religion. With 5.5 million members (53% of Sweden's population), the Church of Sweden is the world's second-largest Lutheran denomination after the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America, and the first major Protestant church to ordain women to the episcopate (bishop).

Gustav Vasa's 1527 Reformation was primarily fiscal: the Swedish state was indebted and the Church's property wealth (25% of Swedish agricultural land) was confiscated to pay military debts. Archbishop Gustav Trolle, who had supported the Danish king against Sweden, was deposed; the church was subordinated to the crown. The Reformation reached Sweden largely as a state administrative reform before deep theological transformation, creating a church with Catholic liturgical continuity and Lutheran theology.

The Church of Sweden's theological progressivism: women's ordination (approved 1960, first bishops ordained 1994); first openly gay bishop (Eva Brunne, Bishop of Stockholm 2009); same-sex marriage blessing (2009). The 2000 separation gave the church full independence: ministers ceased to be civil servants, and the state ceased funding the church through taxes (a 'church fee' replaced the tax). The church maintains responsibility for culturally significant burial grounds, many predating Christian use.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Church of Sweden — established by a fiscal land-grab in 1527 and progressively evolving to ordain women bishops (1994) and gay bishops (2009) — represents the most theologically progressive arc of any major Protestant denomination, demonstrating how a state-church origin can produce the world's most LGBT-inclusive major denomination.
